title: The Sommelier's Nightmare
desc: Obscure origins, chemistry in the kitchen & drinks that fool experts

questions.q: Capsaicin makes chillies hot — but where in the pepper is it actually concentrated?
questions.a: The white pith (placenta), not the seeds as most people think

questions.q: In a famous 1976 wine tasting called 'The Judgment of Paris', what happened that shocked the world?
questions.a: Californian wines beat French wines in a blind tasting judged by French experts

questions.q: Maillard reaction is responsible for browning when you sear meat — but it's technically not caramelisation. What's the key difference?
questions.a: Maillard requires amino acids (proteins) reacting with sugars; caramelisation is sugars alone breaking down

questions.q: What common food is technically classified as a 'modified stem' by botanists — not a root?
questions.a: A potato (it's a tuber, which is a swollen underground stem)

questions.q: MSG was isolated in 1908 by a Japanese chemist from what specific food?
questions.a: Kombu seaweed (kelp broth) — by Kikunae Ikeda

questions.q: Which spirit must legally be aged in new charred oak barrels?
questions.a: Bourbon (not Scotch — Scotch typically uses second-hand bourbon barrels)

questions.q: The 'French Paradox' refers to the puzzling observation that the French have low heart disease rates despite what?
questions.a: A diet high in saturated fats — red wine consumption was proposed as the explanation

questions.q: Vanilla is the second most expensive spice after saffron. What plant family does it belong to?
questions.a: Orchids — vanilla comes from a species of orchid (Vanilla planifolia)

questions.q: What happens chemically when you 'cook' fish in lime juice to make ceviche?
questions.a: The citric acid denatures the proteins — same structural change as heat, but without raising the temperature

questions.q: Blue cheese gets its distinctive veins from what being physically introduced during the aging process?
questions.a: Metal rods or needles are poked through the cheese to create air channels where Penicillium mould can grow
